title: Ethiopian Sweet Ambasha
community: Tigray and northern Ethiopia — the sweetened celebration version
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Sweet Ambasha — the celebration version of Ambasha (ETH005) made with additional honey, more sugar, and enriched with egg. Deeper golden, more fragrant with cardamom, and decorated with the intricate geometric pattern — served as the dessert bread at the most important celebrations.
longDesc: Sweet Ambasha is the dessert version of the everyday Ambasha — made more indulgent with egg, more honey, and a more generous hand with cardamom. It occupies the space between bread and cake, eaten as dessert at celebrations.
ingredients: // Honey glaze: 2 tbsp honey + 1 tsp water
equipment: Large flat pan with lid or oven at 175°C
steps: Dissolve yeast in warm water with 1 tsp honey. Rest 10 minutes.
Beat egg with remaining honey, sugar, and oil.
Combine flour, salt, cardamom, fenugreek, and cinnamon.
Add yeast mixture and egg mixture to flour. Knead 8 minutes.
Press into a large round 2cm thick.
Press deep geometric patterns into the surface.
Pan method: cook covered on medium-low 20 minutes per side.
Or oven: bake at 175°C for 35—40 minutes.
Brush with honey glaze immediately out of the pan/oven.
chefTips: Egg enrichment makes the crumb more tender than standard Ambasha.
More honey than the standard version — the bread should taste noticeably sweet.
The honey glaze gives a beautiful glossy finish.
commonMistakes: Too high heat — the honey content burns easily.
cookingScience: See ETH170 for honey bread baking science. The additional egg in Sweet Ambasha provides lecithin — an emulsifier that creates a more tender crumb by inhibiting gluten development.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian honey from the Tigray highlands.
culturalNote: Sweet Ambasha is the northern Ethiopian celebration bread elevated to dessert — the same geometric pattern, the same fenugreek fragrance, but sweeter, richer, and glazed with honey. At Tigrinya celebrations, it is the sweet conclusion to the meal.
